### Rule 125 : Icon column alignment

**Any icon column (or icon + short text) must be left-aligned.**

Nerd Font icons have variable width depending on the terminal. Left alignment is the only one that guarantees consistent rendering.

| Content type | Alignment |
|-----------------|------------|
| Icon alone | **Left** |
| Icon + short text | **Left** |
| Alphanumeric text | Left (default) |

#### An icon in the first column **is** a column

When a `datatable`'s first column carries a glyph, it is a column in its own
right — not a prefix stuck onto the neighboring text cell.

| | |
|---|---|
| Title | **empty**. The glyph reads in a glance; a header would be naming something that does not need naming, and `eza` does not put one there either. |
| Width | `datatable.IconColumnWidth` (2): the glyph, plus one cell so it does not touch the text. Two, not one — a Nerd Font glyph renders double-width on some terminals, and a single cell would truncate it there. |
| `Sizing` | `SizingFixed`. Nothing to measure. |
| `Less` / `Search` | **none**. It adds no text anyone could type, so filtering stays on the name columns; and a comparator would cost two more cells to fit its sort arrow. |

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — the glyph has its own column
{
    Title: "", Sizing: datatable.SizingFixed, MinWidth: datatable.IconColumnWidth,
    Cell: func(r row) string { return r.icon() },
},
{
    Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 16,
    Cell:   func(r row) string { return r.Name },
    Search: func(r row) string { return r.Name },
},

// ❌ WRONG — the glyph stuck into the identifying column
{
    Title: "Name", Sizing: datatable.SizingContent, MinWidth: 18,
    Cell: func(r row) string { return theme.IconDocker + " " + r.Name },
},
```

**What sticking it in costs**, and this is what settles it: the identifying
column spends its width on something that is not the name, and a
`SizingContent` then measures the glyph along with it — so the table's most
contested column reserves two cells for an icon, at every width.

#### An icon's color goes through a **role**, never through the glyph

Rule 122 applies here as everywhere: `Cell` renders the bare glyph, `Style`
colors it. What Rule 125 adds is **where the color comes from** —
`theme.IconStyle(role)`, and a role declared in `theme/iconcolors.go`.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — the view names a meaning, the theme answers with a color
Cell:  func(r row) string { return nodeKindIcon(r.node) },
Style: func(r row) lipgloss.Style { return theme.IconStyle(nodeKindRole(r.node)) },

// ❌ WRONG — the view decides the hue
Style: func(r row) lipgloss.Style {
    return lipgloss.NewStyle().Foreground(theme.ColorSecondary)
},
```

**A codepoint is not a name.** A table of `U+F0849 → ColorSecondary` cannot
be reviewed: nothing on the line says whether the entry is correct, so an
error there is indistinguishable from a deliberate choice. A role can be
discussed, which is why it is the key.

The five roles are overridable via a theme file (`icon_namespace`,
`icon_repository`, `icon_vis_*`) — unlike syntax colors, which are closed
aliases: an icon is the first thing seen on a row, so it is the part of the
palette a user is most likely to have an opinion about.

**All three icon tables declare a `Style`** — `ws`, `:sec`, and the
explorer — and a fourth that did not declare one would be the application's
only monochrome icon column. A missing role shows: the cell falls back to
`ColorText` (see `IconColor`), so an oversight renders ordinary text rather
than nothing.

**The same object keeps its color from one view to another.** A git repo is
`IconRoleRepository` in `ws`, in `:sec`, and in the explorer — the role is
shared, not duplicated. This is the property for which the key is a meaning
rather than a glyph: the three views do not even show the same glyph for it.

**The granularity is that of the action, not that of the type.** `ws`
colors in three classes — repo, directory, file — which are exactly the
three branches of `availability.go`, and **not** a shade per language the
way `eza` does: `.go` versus `.rs` changes no shortcut on the row, so the
color would say nothing. An icon column is colored by what the row lets you
do.

**The color disappears under the cursor**, like that of any colored column:
the selected row is rendered whole by `styles.Selected` (Rule 122). An icon
column therefore cannot be the *only* carrier of a piece of information —
which is why the explorer's kind stays readable another way (the glyph
outside selection, the position in the tree inside it).

The three tables concerned are `ws`, `containers`, and the `:sec` inventory,
and they declare the same constant. `TestAnIconColumnIsUntitledAndTwoCellsWide`
(`internal/ui/datatable`) scans the sources and rejects a titleless column
that invents its own width. It does not see the other half — a glyph stuck
into a text cell is indistinguishable from a name that starts with a
glyph — which stays a matter for review.

#### The activity column

**In a view with long-running operations (jobs, agents, containers), the first
column is the activity indicator.** It is built by `datatable.IndicatorColumn`,
never by a literal `Column` with an `Indicator` field set (`TestOnlyIndicatorColumnSetsIndicator`
rejects it). It keeps the icon-column shape above: untitled, `SizingFixed`,
`datatable.IconColumnWidth`. When the row is at rest (`indicator.Idle`) the
cell shows the row's own icon via its `theme.IconStyle` role, or an empty cell.

- **The color says the state, never the operation.** A scan, a clone and a
  `docker stop` that are running all look the same: `●` / `○`. What is being
  done is the footer's and the Jobs view's business.
- **No green for "done".** `Done` is `◉` in `ColorActivityNeutral`. Green stays
  reserved for the exceptions Rule 122 lists.
- **The colors are closed aliases**, assigned in `ApplyTheme`:
  `ColorActivityRunning`, `ColorActivityNeutral`, `ColorActivitySuspended`,
  `ColorActivityFailed`. They are not `icon_*` roles and no theme file gains a
  key: a theme that retuned them per state would break the one alphabet of
  states the application shares.
- **The glyph carries the meaning, the color repeats it.** Under the cursor
  the color is repainted on `ColorTableLineSelected` and the glyph still reads.
- **The blink phase is read at render.** The view's tick calls
  `m.table.SetBlinkPhase(on)`; nothing is rebuilt. Without the call the phase
  is on: a running row shows a steady `●`.

Forbidden:
- ❌ A literal `Column{Indicator: …}` instead of `datatable.IndicatorColumn`
- ❌ A glyph literal (`"●"`, `"⊗"`) in a view: use `indicator.Glyph`
- ❌ A color chosen in the view for an activity state
- ❌ Green for a finished operation
- ❌ A color that depends on the type of operation

Forbidden:
- ❌ `.Align(lipgloss.Center)` on an icon column
- ❌ `.Align(lipgloss.Right)` on an icon column
- ❌ A title above a glyph column
- ❌ A local width (`colIconFixed`, `statusColumnWidth`, a literal `2`) instead of `datatable.IconColumnWidth`
- ❌ A glyph prefixed inside a text column's cell
- ❌ An icon color chosen in the view instead of a `theme.IconStyle` role
- ❌ A color table indexed by the glyph rather than by meaning
- ❌ An icon column with no `Style`, while the other three have one
- ❌ A role per file type where the row offers the same actions

### Rule 139 : A `datatable`'s body is never replaced — not by a spinner, not by a message

**A `datatable` stays a table, whatever it contains.** Whether it is
loading its data, empty because nothing has run yet, or empty because a
filter no longer matches anything, the rendered body is always
`m.table.View()` — header included, no rows. `datatable.View()` already
does this on its own: a zero-element table renders its header and fills
the rest with the background (`internal/ui/datatable/render.go`). Nothing
in a view therefore needs to detect this case.

What a body would have said instead — loading, the row count, a verdict —
is **the footer's and header's business**, never the body's:

- loading is a `components.Status{Text: "...", Spinner: true}` in the
  footer (Rule 128);
- the row count, or whatever stands in for it (a verdict, a total), is a
  field of `GetHeaderInfo` (`shortcut.HeaderInfo{Key: "Images", Value: "0"}`) —
  it, not the body, answers "what am I looking at."

**Why.** A body that substitutes itself for the table — with a spinner or
with text — loses its header and its columns for as long as the condition
holds, then regains them: the layout jumps on every refresh, every
`ctrl+r`, every keystroke in the filter. The header and the footer, on the
other hand, have a fixed height (Rule 124): what they display changes
without ever moving the table.

```go
// ✅ CORRECT — the body is always the table; the footer and header speak
func (m Model) renderImagesView() string {
    return m.imageTable.View()
}

func (m Model) status() sharedcomponents.Status {
    if text, ok := m.loadingLabel(); ok {
        return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: text, Spinner: true}
    }
    return sharedcomponents.Status{Text: m.actionLine()}
}

func (m Model) GetHeaderInfo(_ string) []shortcut.HeaderInfo {
    return []shortcut.HeaderInfo{
        {Key: "Images", Value: fmt.Sprintf("%d", len(m.imageTable.Visible())), Style: theme.HeaderValueStyle},
    }
}

// ❌ WRONG — the body replaces itself with a spinner
if m.loading && len(m.images) == 0 {
    return theme.SpinnerMessage(m.spinner.View(), "Loading images...")
}

// ❌ WRONG — the body replaces itself with a message, empty or filtered
if len(m.imageTable.Visible()) == 0 {
    return theme.DimStyle.Render("No images found")
}
```

The spinner's frame is pushed from the `spinner.TickMsg` handler:
`m.footer.SetSpinnerFrame(m.spinner.View())`. Without this call the spinner
stays on frame zero, which reads as a hang.

`TestNoTableViewRendersALoadingBody` (`internal/ui/components`) rejects a
`theme.SpinnerMessage` in table views. An operation screen with no table
behind it (a `docker pull` in progress) is an exception **declared in the
test**.

**Declared exception: a welcome screen, not a status message.** The empty
`:sec` inventory (`internal/ui/security/inventory.go`, `renderEmptyInventory`)
replaces the body with a paragraph that explains *where scans come from* —
this is not "0 rows," it is first-use onboarding, with more content than a
header field can carry. The distinction: a message that fits in
`GetHeaderInfo` (a count, a status) goes there; text that explains an
entire application flow stays an explicit exception, like the one already
provided for loading.

### Rule 136 : Filter Bar for Tables

**Every table view must use `components.FilterBar` for search and toggle filters. No ad-hoc filter implementations.**

#### Behaviour

| State | Bar visible | Description |
|-------|-------------|-------------|
| No filter | ❌ | Bar is completely hidden |
| Toggle filter active | ✅ | Bar shows dimmed placeholder + active token(s) |
| Search mode (after `/`) | ✅ | Bar shows focused text input + active token(s) |
| Search confirmed (query set) | ✅ | Bar shows dimmed placeholder + query token + toggle tokens |

#### Visual

The filter bar forms a **closed rectangle** that visually connects with the viewport's bottom border:

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────┐   ← viewport top border
│  table rows...                          │
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘   ← viewport bottom border (= rectangle top)
│  / cursor...         [tcp]  ·  [LISTEN] │   ← content line with │ sides
└─────────────────────────────────────────┘   ← rectangle bottom border
```

Both lines use `theme.ColorViewportBorder` for `│`, `└`, `┘`, `─` characters.

#### Placement — Footer, not viewport

The filter bar is rendered in `RenderFooter()`, **not** in the viewport content.

- `GetFooterHeight()` returns `baseFooterHeight + filterBar.ExtraHeight()`
- `RenderFooter()` prepends `filterBar.View()` when `filterBar.IsVisible()`
- Table height formula does **not** subtract `filterBar.ExtraHeight()` — the app router handles that via `GetFooterHeight()`

#### Integration Pattern

```go
// In Model struct
filterBar components.FilterBar  // or components.NewFilterBarWithTokens(tokens)

// In GetFooterHeight()
func (m Model) GetFooterHeight() int {
    return 2 + m.filterBar.ExtraHeight() // base (empty line + info) + filter bar
}

// In RenderFooter()
func (m Model) RenderFooter(width int) string {
    var parts []string
    if m.filterBar.IsVisible() {
        parts = append(parts, m.filterBar.View())
    }
    parts = append(parts, theme.EmptyLineBg(width), infoLine)
    return strings.Join(parts, "\n")
}

// In resize() / WindowSizeMsg handler — NO ExtraHeight subtraction
tableHeight := m.height - overhead  // overhead = header row only, NOT filterBar.ExtraHeight()
m.table.SetHeight(tableHeight)

// In Update() / key handler — forward keys when in search mode
if m.filterBar.InEditMode() {
    m.filterBar, cmd = m.filterBar.Update(msg)
    m.applyFilters()
    return m, cmd
}
// "/" key activates search
case "/":
    return m, m.filterBar.ActivateSearch()

// In InEditMode() — propagate to app router
func (m Model) InEditMode() bool {
    return m.filterBar.InEditMode() || /* other edit states */
}

// In View() / renderNormalView() — table only, NO filter bar here
func (m Model) renderNormalView() string {
    return m.table.View()
}

// In applyFilters() — use filterBar.SearchQuery() for text filtering
query := strings.ToLower(m.filterBar.SearchQuery())
```

#### Toggle filter tokens (views with dedicated filter keys)

Use `components.NewFilterBarWithTokens()` and update token active state when toggle keys are pressed:

```go
// Init
fb := components.NewFilterBarWithTokens([]components.FilterToken{
    {Label: "tcp"},
    {Label: "udp"},
})

// On key "t"
fb.SetTokenActive("tcp", !fb.IsTokenActive("tcp"))
```

#### Rules

- ✅ Use `components.FilterBar` — never re-implement the filter bar locally
- ✅ The frame itself is `components.BarFrame(width, inner)`: that is what
  `FilterBar.View()` calls, and the only path for whatever shares this slot
  without being a filter — the viewer's go-to-line prompt (§3.53). Two
  implementations of the rectangle would be free to diverge on where the
  corners sit.
- ✅ Only one occupant of the slot at a time, and the height does not depend
  on which one — otherwise the panel resizes under the reader whenever one
  opens on top of the other.
- ✅ `filterBar.ExtraHeight()` must be added to `GetFooterHeight()` return value
- ✅ `filterBar.View()` must be prepended in `RenderFooter()` when `filterBar.IsVisible()`
- ✅ `filterBar.InEditMode()` must propagate via the view's `InEditMode()` method
- ✅ `"/"` key must always call `filterBar.ActivateSearch()`
- ❌ Filter bar must NOT be rendered inside the viewport (`View()` / `renderNormalView()`)
- ❌ `filterBar.ExtraHeight()` must NOT be subtracted from table height (app router handles it)
- ❌ `filterInput textinput.Model` fields in view models (use FilterBar instead)

The following MCP servers have provided instructions for how to use their tools and resources:

## claude.ai Claude Docs
Claude Docs: living docs you create and edit here. A docs skill your client lists → load it before any docs call — also before a `read`, comment or tab change on a claude.ai …/artifact/… link (the link is a doc; never web-fetch it). No docs skill or guide text loaded → `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )` alone before any docs call but a doc's birth. Make a doc here — not a local file, even when coding — only when the user asks for one, and make it FIRST: the turn's first tool call is its skeleton (title, byline, a `pending` block per section) — a reflex: send it before any search, file read, plan, `guide` or thinking it through; think once it is open — `batch( container = {"kind":"project","create":{"name":"<title>","doc":{"blocks":{"asof":{"type":"date","value":"<today>"},"me":{"type":"mention","user":"me"},"s1":{"type":"pending","intent":"Goals: the three outcomes this quarter commits to"},"s2":{…}},"markdown":"# <title>\n\n<?claude block asof?> · <?claude block me?>\n\n<?claude block s1?>\n\n<?claude block s2?>"}}}, batch = [] )` (`<?claude block k?>` ↔ `blocks.k`); its ack links the doc → `open` it with your Artifact tool (none → start your next message with the link, once); they're likely watching it fill — keep them posted in a short line naming what you're on (outline up; now <topic>); findings go in the doc, not chat; then `guide( items = ["topic.index"] )`, research, and fill each section: `replace` its pending id with `## <heading>` + body; end with one line + the link, never the document. Summoned by a doc comment (turn headed `[Artifact comment sent to Claude]`, `;thread=<root id>`): answer ONLY with a doc comment under that root (`create` an utterance, parent `<root id>`) — no artifact/platform comment tool: that relay thread is resolved and never reaches the doc; an edit asked there → `update` with `answering: "<root id>"`.

## Epics

There are no epic tools — an epic is a work item whose type is named "Epic". Work
items always belong to a project; ask which if one is not named.
1. type = `workitem_type resolve` with project_id and name="Epic" — type.id is the type_id.
2. Create: `workitem create` with project_id, type_id=type.id, name=...
3. List: `workitem list` with project_id and pql='type = "<type id>"'.
4. Read / update / delete / nest: `workitem retrieve` / `workitem update` /
   `workitem delete` by work item id (set parent=<work item id> to nest).
5. List an epic's children: `workitem list` with pql='childOf("<EPIC-IDENTIFIER>")'
   using the epic's human-readable identifier (e.g. "PROJ-12") from `workitem retrieve`.

## plugin:dev-team:context7
Use this server to fetch current documentation whenever the user asks about a library, framework, SDK, API, CLI tool, or cloud service — even well-known ones like React, Next.js, Prisma, Express, Tailwind, Django, or Spring Boot. This includes API syntax, configuration, version migration, porting code between libraries, platforms, or SQL dialects, library-specific debugging, setup instructions, and CLI tool usage. Use even when you think you know the answer — your training data may not reflect recent changes. Prefer this over web search for library docs.

Do not use for: refactoring, debugging, or reviewing code that does not depend on a library or platform API, or general programming concepts.

1	# DEVDESK-139 — Shared blink tick (A-03)
2	
3	Story A-03 (`docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md`), Plane DEVDESK-139, epic E1.
4	Depends on A-01 (DEVDESK-137, shipped: `datatable.SetBlinkPhase`, `indicator`) and sits
5	beside A-04 (DEVDESK-138, shipped: `ChangedMsg.Failures`). Inputs: `stories.md` (A-03, D2,
6	D7, annex R3/R8/R10/Q1), `brief.md` (H2), `app-shell.md` ("The broadcast, and the one
7	spinner chain"), `internal/app/jobs.go`, `internal/app/app.go`. One PR, effort M (high risk:
8	the router's `Update`).
9	
10	**No view blinks after this PR.** No view has an `IndicatorColumn` or implements
11	`WantsBlink` yet (A-06 is the first). What changes on screen: nothing, if the footer and
12	row spinners keep moving — which is the risk this plan is organised around.
13	
14	## Blocking questions (user)
15	
16	**Q1. Criterion 8 names `TEA_TRACE`, which does not exist in the Bubble Tea DevDesk uses.**
17	Verified in the module source (`bubbletea@v1.3.10`): no `TEA_TRACE`, no `os.Getenv` at
18	all. `research.md` cites it from a documentation page that describes another version. In
19	addition, no view blinks before A-06, so "1 and 20 blinking rows" cannot be read off the
20	real application in this PR.
21	
22	- **A (recommended).** An in-process measurement, opt-in: `TestMeasureRedrawCost` in
23	  `internal/app`, skipped unless `DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1`. It runs a real `tea.Program`
24	  on the real router (header, viewport frame) with `tea.WithOutput(countingWriter)`,
25	  `tea.WithInput(nil)`, at 120×40, a fake view holding a `datatable` with an
26	  `IndicatorColumn` and N Running rows, for 10 s, and logs bytes/s for N = 0, 1, 20 at
27	  1 Hz — plus, for reference, the same rows under today's 10 Hz frame. Those bytes are
28	  exactly what the renderer would send over SSH. Numbers go in the PR body. Step 6.
29	- **B.** Measure on a real terminal only, with `script -q -f` (util-linux) recording the
30	  output of `bin/dk`, over SSH. Needs a blinking view, so it moves to A-06; criterion 8
31	  of A-03 is then reworded.
32	- **C.** A production hook (`DEVDESK_TRACE_OUTPUT=…` wrapping stdout in a counting
33	  writer in `main.go`). Not recommended: shipped code for a one-off measurement.
34	
35	A does not exclude a real SSH check at the A-06 checkpoint, where H2 is consigned anyway.
36	
37	**Q2. Criterion 4 ("in the whole application, one tick animates rows") cannot be true
38	when A-03 lands.** Four row-animation chains outside the router remain, each removed by a
39	later story: `oci_resources/busy.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-09b), `containers/update.go`
40	(`AdvanceSpinner`, A-14), `netdiag/ports_model.go` (`portsSpinnerCmd`, A-12), the OCI
41	registry browser's `tagScanSpinnerIdx` (A-09a).
42	
43	- **A (recommended).** A-03 makes the router side true (one chain, renamed "animation",
44	  and only the router builds a `jobs.FrameMsg`) and adds a source test that names those
45	  four as **declared exceptions** which may only disappear (a stale exception fails the
46	  test). This pulls a thin slice of A-16 forward; A-16 later absorbs it.
47	- **B.** Router side only; the application-wide check waits for A-16 (A-06's PR). The
48	  criterion is then met in A-16, not here.
49	- **C.** Remove the four chains in A-03. Overlaps four stories, effort L. Not recommended.
50	
51	Neither question blocks steps 1 to 5; Q1 decides step 6, Q2 decides one test of step 5.
52	
53	## Hypotheses (low consequence, prudent choice taken)
54	
55	- **`app.motion` does not exist** (no `Motion` in `internal/config`; only the legend
56	  text of A-01 mentions it). A-03 adds an unexported router field `motionStatic bool`
57	  (zero value = blink, the A-02 default) and a method `setMotionStatic(bool)`; tests set
58	  it. A-02 wires it from `cfg.App.Motion` at the three points `gauge_glyph` uses (startup,
59	  context switch, `ConfigSavedMsg`). Nothing is read from YAML here.
60	- **Only the view on screen is asked `WantsBlink()`**, not every held view (the annex
61	  R3 said "vues tenues"). Reason: criterion 7 sends the frame to the view on screen only,
62	  so a tick kept alive for an off-screen view would animate nothing; a view entering the
63	  screen is asked at the end of the very `Update` that switched to it (level signal).
64	  Stricter for criterion 2, and reversible in one line.
65	- **`Frame`/`RenderedFrame` leave `jobs.ChangedMsg`** and move to `jobs.FrameMsg`. This
66	  reverses the comment on `ChangedMsg` ("one message and not two"), on purpose: the
67	  compiler then finds every reader of the frame, which is the protection against a view
68	  whose spinner freezes because it only handled `ChangedMsg`.
69	- **The chain uses `tea.Every`, not `tea.Tick`.** `tea.Every` fires on the clock's
70	  boundaries (`n.Truncate(d).Add(d)`), so a 500 ms chain ticks just after each half
71	  period and `(t.UnixMilli()/500)%2` alternates strictly. With `tea.Tick` the drift
72	  (500 ms + processing) eventually lands two ticks in buckets of the same parity: one
73	  blink skipped, a 1 s steady `●`.
74	- **`datatable.Animating()`** (A-01 hand-off) is not added here: it has no caller until
75	  the first view implementing `WantsBlink` (A-09b / A-10a / A-13 / A-14). It goes with it.
76	- **Measurement results** (Q1 A) go in the PR body and in one entry of `docs/journal.md`;
77	  nothing in `docs/architecture/`.
78	- **No ADR file**: the project records lasting decisions in `docs/backlog.md`. Step 7
79	  adds the next D number (D96 at the time of writing) for "frame/phase split from the
80	  registry snapshot, level-signalled blink, `Update` wrapper".
81	
82	## Target design (summary)
83	
84	```
85	App.Update(msg)                      // new wrapper, the only exported entry
86	  ├─ a.update(msg)                   // today's switch, unchanged
87	  └─ a.ensureTick()                  // level signal, every message
88	
89	ensureTick: cadence(Running()>0, view on screen WantsBlink(), motionStatic)
90	  fast 100 ms  if Running()>0                 (footer spinners depend on the frame)
91	  blink 500 ms if WantsBlink && !motionStatic
92	  none         otherwise → a live chain dies at its next tick
93	  starts a chain if none, or REPLACES a slower one (seq++); never a second one
94	
95	handleAnimationTick(seq, at):
96	  stale seq → dropped, no Cmd
97	  none      → ticking=false; if phase was off: pin on + FrameMsg to view on screen
98	  else      → frame++ (only if Running()>0); blinkOn = motionStatic || phase(at)
99	              FrameMsg → view on screen only; renew at the cadence wanted now
100	switchView → ChangedMsg (snapshot) + FrameMsg (current frame and phase)
101	jobsChanged → ChangedMsg to every held view + FrameMsg to the view on screen + ensureTick
102	```
103	
104	---
105	
106	## Step 1 — phase and cadence, pure functions · S · parallel with 2
107	
108	**Files:** new `internal/app/animation.go`, new `internal/app/animation_test.go`.
109	
110	```go
111	// blinkHalfPeriod is the blink's half period (D7: 1 Hz). A const: the phase formula
112	// must not change when a test shortens the chain's interval.
113	const blinkHalfPeriod = 500 * time.Millisecond
114	
115	// blinkPhase reads the phase off the tick's own time: on = (ms/500) % 2 == 0.
116	func blinkPhase(t time.Time) bool
117	
118	// cadence returns the interval the animation chain should run at, and false when
119	// nothing needs it. running: jobs.Registry.Running() > 0.
120	func cadence(running, wantsBlink, motionStatic bool) (time.Duration, bool)
121	
122	// Intervals are vars so testutil.FastTimers can shorten them (as jobSpinnerInterval was).
123	var (
124	    animationFastInterval  = spinner.Dot.FPS  // 100 ms, unchanged
125	    animationBlinkInterval = blinkHalfPeriod  // 500 ms
126	)
127	```
128	
129	**Tests (write first):**
130	- `TestThePhaseIsReadFromTheTickTime` (table): `UnixMilli` 0 → on, 499 → on, 500 → off,
131	  999 → off, 1000 → on, 1_700_000_000_250 → on, …_750 → off.
132	- `TestTheCadence` (table): running → fast whatever the rest; !running+wants+!static →
133	  blink; !running+wants+static → none; !running+!wants → none; running+static → fast.
134	
135	**Done when:** `go test ./internal/app/ -run 'Phase|Cadence'` passes.

137	## Step 2 — `jobs.FrameMsg` and its readers in the views · M · parallel with 1; per-view sub-steps parallelisable
138	
139	Additive: `ChangedMsg` still carries the frame, the router still broadcasts it on each
140	tick. After this step every reader also understands `FrameMsg`.
141	
142	**Files:** `internal/jobs/message.go`, `internal/jobs/message_test.go` (if present) and
143	one `case jobs.FrameMsg:` + handler per reader:
144	
145	| View | File(s) | `handleFrame(msg jobs.FrameMsg)` does |
146	|---|---|---|
147	| workspaces | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | `jobFrame`, `footer.SetSpinnerFrame(RenderedFrame)`, `refreshRows()` |
148	| security | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | `jobFrame`, `setInventory(m.inventory.Items())` |
149	| oci_resources | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | `jobFrame`, `updateImageTable()` (footer untouched, as today) |
150	| jobsview | `update.go` | `frame`, footer, `refreshRows()` |
151	| forge/explorer | `update.go`, `clone.go` | `jobFrame`, footer; clone open → `clone.setRun(clone.run, Frame)`, else `updateTableRows()` |
152	| filebrowser | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | footer only |
153	| templates | `update.go`, `scan.go` | footer only |
154	| dashboard | `model.go` | footer only |
155	
156	```go
157	// FrameMsg says the animation moved: the spinner frame, the blink phase, or both.
158	// It carries no snapshot — ChangedMsg is for changes of the registry. The router
159	// sends it to the view on screen only, on every tick and when a view enters.
160	type FrameMsg struct {
161	    Frame         string // bare, Rule 122 (a cell measures it)
162	    RenderedFrame string // styled, Rule 128 (a footer takes it)
163	    Blink         bool   // true = ● ; pinned true with app.motion: static or no chain
164	}
165	```
166	
167	No view calls `SetBlinkPhase` yet (no `IndicatorColumn` in any view; A-06 adds the first).
168	
169	**Tests (write first), one or two per package, named alike:**
170	- `TestAFrameMovesTheRowSpinner` (workspaces, security, oci_resources, jobsview,
171	  explorer tree and clone list): a running target, `ChangedMsg{Runs}` then
172	  `FrameMsg{Frame: "X"}` → the row's cell shows `X`; a second `FrameMsg{Frame: "Y"}` →
173	  `Y`, runs unchanged.
174	- `TestAFrameMovesTheFooterSpinner` (workspaces, jobsview, explorer, filebrowser,
175	  templates, dashboard): a running run, `FrameMsg{RenderedFrame: "R"}` → `RenderFooter`
176	  contains `R`.
177	- `TestAFrameKeepsTheSnapshot` (one package suffices, workspaces): `FrameMsg` does not
178	  reset `m.jobs`/failures held from the last `ChangedMsg`.
179	
180	**Done when:** `go test ./internal/jobs/ ./internal/ui/workspaces/ ./internal/ui/security/
181	./internal/ui/oci_resources/ ./internal/ui/jobsview/ ./internal/ui/forge/explorer/
182	./internal/ui/filebrowser/ ./internal/ui/templates/ ./internal/ui/dashboard/` passes.
183	
184	## Step 3 — the router chain renamed "animation"; the tick sends `FrameMsg` only · M · after 1 and 2
185	
186	**Files:** `internal/app/animation.go` (chain moved out of `jobs.go`), `internal/app/jobs.go`,
187	`internal/app/app.go` (fields, `case`), `internal/app/command_line.go` (`switchView`),
188	`internal/jobs/message.go` (drop `Frame`/`RenderedFrame` from `ChangedMsg`, rewrite its
189	comment), the eight `handleJobsChanged` (drop their frame lines — the compiler lists
190	them), tests: `internal/app/jobs_test.go`, `failures_test.go`, `forge_index_test.go`
191	(`jobSpinnerInterval` → `animationFastInterval`), and the view tests that put `Frame`
192	in a `ChangedMsg` (`jobsview_test.go` ×4, `security_jobs_test.go` ×2,
193	`explorer/model_test.go` ×2, `dashboard_test.go`, `oci_resources/jobs_test.go`,
194	`workspaces_test.go`) → send a `FrameMsg` instead.
195	
196	Renames (D2): `jobTickMsg` → `animationTickMsg{seq int; at time.Time}`, `ensureJobTick`
197	→ `ensureTick`, `handleJobTick` → `handleAnimationTick`, `jobTick` → `animationTick`,
198	`jobFrame` → `animationFrame`, fields `jobFrameIdx/jobTickSeq/jobTicking` →
199	
200	```go
201	// animation is the one chain that moves anything on a row (D5, renamed D2).
202	type animationState struct {
203	    seq      int           // identifies the live chain; a tick from another is dropped
204	    ticking  bool
205	    interval time.Duration // cadence of the live chain
206	    frameIdx int
207	    blinkOn  bool          // starts true (newWithSize); true whenever no chain runs
208	}
209	
210	// animationEvery is tea.Every, a var so tests record the interval and inject the time
211	// without sleeping. Never captured by a Cmd with `a` (Rule 110): seq and interval by value.
212	var animationEvery = tea.Every
213	
214	func animationTick(seq int, d time.Duration) tea.Cmd   // animationEvery(d, func(t) { return animationTickMsg{seq, t} })
215	func (a *App) frameMsg() jobs.FrameMsg                  // frame bare + styled + a.anim.blinkOn
216	func (a *App) sendFrameTo(target command.ViewType) tea.Cmd // like sendJobsTo, no resize
217	```
218	
219	In this step `ensureTick` still keys on `Running() > 0` only, at `animationFastInterval`
220	(behaviour of today). `handleAnimationTick`: stale seq → `nil`; `Running()==0` → stop;
221	else `frameIdx++` and `tea.Batch(a.sendFrameTo(a.currentView), animationTick(seq, d))` —
222	**no `broadcastJobs()` on a tick any more**. `switchView` batches `sendJobsTo(view)` then
223	`sendFrameTo(view)`. `jobsChanged()` = `broadcastJobs()` + `sendFrameTo(a.currentView)` +
224	`ensureTick()`.
225	
226	**Tests (write first; existing ones renamed where they cover the same thing):**
227	- `TestOnlyOneAnimationChainIsEverAlive` (was `TestOnlyOneSpinnerChainIsEverAlive`).
228	- `TestATickFromAnOlderChainIsDropped` (kept, on `animationTickMsg`): no frame change,
229	  `cmd == nil`, no `FrameMsg` delivered.
230	- `TestATickSendsAFrameAndNoSnapshot`: two held fake views, a run; after a tick the view
231	  on screen got exactly one more `FrameMsg` and no new `ChangedMsg`; the other got
232	  nothing.
233	- `TestTheFrameIsBareAndItsRenderingIsNot` (was `…BroadcastFrame…`, now on `FrameMsg`).
234	- `TestAViewEnteringTheScreenGetsTheSnapshotAndTheFrame`: `switchView` → the view
235	  receives a `ChangedMsg` then a `FrameMsg` whose `Blink == a.anim.blinkOn`.
236	- `TestARegistryChangeStillReachesEveryView` (existing broadcast test, adapted): a
237	  `StartMsg` → every held view gets a `ChangedMsg`; the view on screen also a `FrameMsg`.
238	- `TestTheChainRunsWhileWorkDoesAndRestartsAfterwards` (kept, adapted: asserts a
239	  `FrameMsg` instead of a second snapshot).
240	
241	**Done when:** `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/app/ ./internal/jobs/ ./internal/ui/...`
242	pass; `grep -rn "\.RenderedFrame\|msg\.Frame" internal/ui` only hits `FrameMsg` handlers.
243	
244	## Step 4 — `BlinkingView`, the `Update` wrapper, the two cadences, `motionStatic` · M · after 3
245	
246	**Files:** `internal/app/app.go` (interface, wrapper, `motionStatic`), `internal/app/animation.go`,
247	`internal/app/harness_test.go` (comment listing probed interfaces; a `blinkingView` fake:
248	`fakeView` + `wants bool`), new `internal/app/animation_router_test.go`.
249	
250	```go
251	// BlinkingView is implemented by a view with a row that blinks for a reason the
252	// registry does not know: an instant action (busy), an agent running, a group's
253	// children loading. Asked after every Update — a level, not an edge (R3).
254	type BlinkingView interface {
255	    WantsBlink() bool
256	}
257	
258	// Update is the router's only entry: the dispatch, then the level check of the
259	// animation chain. update is today's switch, unchanged.
260	func (a *App) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
261	    model, cmd := a.update(msg)
262	    return model, tea.Batch(cmd, a.ensureTick())
263	}
264	
265	func (a *App) wantsBlink() bool          // view on screen implements BlinkingView && WantsBlink()
266	func (a *App) setMotionStatic(on bool)   // A-02 calls it; true pins blinkOn and stops blink-only chains
267	```
268	
269	`ensureTick`: `d, ok := cadence(a.jobs.Running() > 0, a.wantsBlink(), a.motionStatic)`;
270	`!ok` → `nil`; `ticking && interval <= d` → `nil`; else `seq++`, `ticking = true`,
271	`interval = d`, return `animationTick(seq, d)` (replaces a slower chain: criterion 3).
272	`handleAnimationTick`: cadence `!ok` → `ticking = false`; if `!blinkOn` → `blinkOn = true`
273	and `sendFrameTo(currentView)` (a row is never left on `○`); else frame advances only when
274	`Running() > 0`, `blinkOn = motionStatic || blinkPhase(msg.at)`, `interval = d`, FrameMsg to
275	the view on screen, renew at `d` (downgrade 100 → 500 happens here, no new seq).
276	
277	Tests use a stub: `stubAnimationClock(t, at time.Time) *[]time.Duration` swaps
278	`animationEvery` for a function that records `d` and returns a Cmd yielding the tick at
279	`at` immediately (restored in `t.Cleanup`; internal/app has no `t.Parallel`).
280	
281	**Tests (write first):**
282	- Criterion 1 — `TestEveryRowReadsThePhaseOfTheTick`: blinking view on screen, ticks at
283	  `UnixMilli` 1000/1500/2000 → `FrameMsg.Blink` true/false/true; `switchView` to another
284	  blinking view hands it the same `blinkOn`.
285	- Criterion 2 — `TestTheChainDiesWhenNothingAnimates`: blink chain alive, view's `wants`
286	  → false; next tick returns no `animationTickMsg`, `ticking == false`; then ten
287	  `Update(tea.KeyMsg)` record no interval (no periodic message).
288	- Criterion 2 — `TestAStoppedChainLeavesThePhaseOn`: chain dies on an "off" phase → the
289	  view gets a last `FrameMsg{Blink: true}`.
290	- Criterion 3 — `TestAnOperationStartedAfterTheChainDiedRestartsItOnce`: dead chain,
291	  `Update(jobs.StartMsg)` → exactly one interval recorded (100 ms); another `Update` → none.

# DEVDESK-139 — Shared blink tick (A-03)

Story A-03 (`docs/product/activity-indicator/stories.md`), Plane DEVDESK-139, epic E1.
Depends on A-01 (DEVDESK-137, shipped: `datatable.SetBlinkPhase`, `indicator`) and sits
beside A-04 (DEVDESK-138, shipped: `ChangedMsg.Failures`). Inputs: `stories.md` (A-03, D2,
D7, annex R3/R8/R10/Q1), `brief.md` (H2), `app-shell.md` ("The broadcast, and the one
spinner chain"), `internal/app/jobs.go`, `internal/app/app.go`. One PR, effort M (high risk:
the router's `Update`).

**No view blinks after this PR.** No view has an `IndicatorColumn` or implements
`WantsBlink` yet (A-06 is the first). What changes on screen: nothing, if the footer and
row spinners keep moving — which is the risk this plan is organised around.

## Blocking questions (user)

**Q1. Criterion 8 names `TEA_TRACE`, which does not exist in the Bubble Tea DevDesk uses.**
Verified in the module source (`bubbletea@v1.3.10`): no `TEA_TRACE`, no `os.Getenv` at
all. `research.md` cites it from a documentation page that describes another version. In
addition, no view blinks before A-06, so "1 and 20 blinking rows" cannot be read off the
real application in this PR.

- **A (recommended).** An in-process measurement, opt-in: `TestMeasureRedrawCost` in
  `internal/app`, skipped unless `DEVDESK_MEASURE_REDRAW=1`. It runs a real `tea.Program`
  on the real router (header, viewport frame) with `tea.WithOutput(countingWriter)`,
  `tea.WithInput(nil)`, at 120×40, a fake view holding a `datatable` with an
  `IndicatorColumn` and N Running rows, for 10 s, and logs bytes/s for N = 0, 1, 20 at
  1 Hz — plus, for reference, the same rows under today's 10 Hz frame. Those bytes are
  exactly what the renderer would send over SSH. Numbers go in the PR body. Step 6.
- **B.** Measure on a real terminal only, with `script -q -f` (util-linux) recording the
  output of `bin/dk`, over SSH. Needs a blinking view, so it moves to A-06; criterion 8
  of A-03 is then reworded.
- **C.** A production hook (`DEVDESK_TRACE_OUTPUT=…` wrapping stdout in a counting
  writer in `main.go`). Not recommended: shipped code for a one-off measurement.

A does not exclude a real SSH check at the A-06 checkpoint, where H2 is consigned anyway.

**Q2. Criterion 4 ("in the whole application, one tick animates rows") cannot be true
when A-03 lands.** Four row-animation chains outside the router remain, each removed by a
later story: `oci_resources/busy.go` (`AdvanceSpinner`, A-09b), `containers/update.go`
(`AdvanceSpinner`, A-14), `netdiag/ports_model.go` (`portsSpinnerCmd`, A-12), the OCI
registry browser's `tagScanSpinnerIdx` (A-09a).

- **A (recommended).** A-03 makes the router side true (one chain, renamed "animation",
  and only the router builds a `jobs.FrameMsg`) and adds a source test that names those
  four as **declared exceptions** which may only disappear (a stale exception fails the
  test). This pulls a thin slice of A-16 forward; A-16 later absorbs it.
- **B.** Router side only; the application-wide check waits for A-16 (A-06's PR). The
  criterion is then met in A-16, not here.
- **C.** Remove the four chains in A-03. Overlaps four stories, effort L. Not recommended.

Neither question blocks steps 1 to 5; Q1 decides step 6, Q2 decides one test of step 5.

## Hypotheses (low consequence, prudent choice taken)

- **`app.motion` does not exist** (no `Motion` in `internal/config`; only the legend
  text of A-01 mentions it). A-03 adds an unexported router field `motionStatic bool`
  (zero value = blink, the A-02 default) and a method `setMotionStatic(bool)`; tests set
  it. A-02 wires it from `cfg.App.Motion` at the three points `gauge_glyph` uses (startup,
  context switch, `ConfigSavedMsg`). Nothing is read from YAML here.
- **Only the view on screen is asked `WantsBlink()`**, not every held view (the annex
  R3 said "vues tenues"). Reason: criterion 7 sends the frame to the view on screen only,
  so a tick kept alive for an off-screen view would animate nothing; a view entering the
  screen is asked at the end of the very `Update` that switched to it (level signal).
  Stricter for criterion 2, and reversible in one line.
- **`Frame`/`RenderedFrame` leave `jobs.ChangedMsg`** and move to `jobs.FrameMsg`. This
  reverses the comment on `ChangedMsg` ("one message and not two"), on purpose: the
  compiler then finds every reader of the frame, which is the protection against a view
  whose spinner freezes because it only handled `ChangedMsg`.
- **The chain uses `tea.Every`, not `tea.Tick`.** `tea.Every` fires on the clock's
  boundaries (`n.Truncate(d).Add(d)`), so a 500 ms chain ticks just after each half
  period and `(t.UnixMilli()/500)%2` alternates strictly. With `tea.Tick` the drift
  (500 ms + processing) eventually lands two ticks in buckets of the same parity: one
  blink skipped, a 1 s steady `●`.
- **`datatable.Animating()`** (A-01 hand-off) is not added here: it has no caller until
  the first view implementing `WantsBlink` (A-09b / A-10a / A-13 / A-14). It goes with it.
- **Measurement results** (Q1 A) go in the PR body and in one entry of `docs/journal.md`;
  nothing in `docs/architecture/`.
- **No ADR file**: the project records lasting decisions in `docs/backlog.md`. Step 7
  adds the next D number (D96 at the time of writing) for "frame/phase split from the
  registry snapshot, level-signalled blink, `Update` wrapper".

## Target design (summary)

```
App.Update(msg)                      // new wrapper, the only exported entry
  ├─ a.update(msg)                   // today's switch, unchanged
  └─ a.ensureTick()                  // level signal, every message

ensureTick: cadence(Running()>0, view on screen WantsBlink(), motionStatic)
  fast 100 ms  if Running()>0                 (footer spinners depend on the frame)
  blink 500 ms if WantsBlink && !motionStatic
  none         otherwise → a live chain dies at its next tick
  starts a chain if none, or REPLACES a slower one (seq++); never a second one

handleAnimationTick(seq, at):
  stale seq → dropped, no Cmd
  none      → ticking=false; if phase was off: pin on + FrameMsg to view on screen
  else      → frame++ (only if Running()>0); blinkOn = motionStatic || phase(at)
              FrameMsg → view on screen only; renew at the cadence wanted now
switchView → ChangedMsg (snapshot) + FrameMsg (current frame and phase)
jobsChanged → ChangedMsg to every held view + FrameMsg to the view on screen + ensureTick
```

---

## Step 1 — phase and cadence, pure functions · S · parallel with 2

**Files:** new `internal/app/animation.go`, new `internal/app/animation_test.go`.

```go
// blinkHalfPeriod is the blink's half period (D7: 1 Hz). A const: the phase formula
// must not change when a test shortens the chain's interval.
const blinkHalfPeriod = 500 * time.Millisecond

// blinkPhase reads the phase off the tick's own time: on = (ms/500) % 2 == 0.
func blinkPhase(t time.Time) bool

// cadence returns the interval the animation chain should run at, and false when
// nothing needs it. running: jobs.Registry.Running() > 0.
func cadence(running, wantsBlink, motionStatic bool) (time.Duration, bool)

// Intervals are vars so testutil.FastTimers can shorten them (as jobSpinnerInterval was).
var (
    animationFastInterval  = spinner.Dot.FPS  // 100 ms, unchanged
    animationBlinkInterval = blinkHalfPeriod  // 500 ms
)
```

**Tests (write first):**
- `TestThePhaseIsReadFromTheTickTime` (table): `UnixMilli` 0 → on, 499 → on, 500 → off,
  999 → off, 1000 → on, 1_700_000_000_250 → on, …_750 → off.
- `TestTheCadence` (table): running → fast whatever the rest; !running+wants+!static →
  blink; !running+wants+static → none; !running+!wants → none; running+static → fast.

**Done when:** `go test ./internal/app/ -run 'Phase|Cadence'` passes.

## Step 2 — `jobs.FrameMsg` and its readers in the views · M · parallel with 1; per-view sub-steps parallelisable

Additive: `ChangedMsg` still carries the frame, the router still broadcasts it on each
tick. After this step every reader also understands `FrameMsg`.

**Files:** `internal/jobs/message.go`, `internal/jobs/message_test.go` (if present) and
one `case jobs.FrameMsg:` + handler per reader:

| View | File(s) | `handleFrame(msg jobs.FrameMsg)` does |
|---|---|---|
| workspaces | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | `jobFrame`, `footer.SetSpinnerFrame(RenderedFrame)`, `refreshRows()` |
| security | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | `jobFrame`, `setInventory(m.inventory.Items())` |
| oci_resources | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | `jobFrame`, `updateImageTable()` (footer untouched, as today) |
| jobsview | `update.go` | `frame`, footer, `refreshRows()` |
| forge/explorer | `update.go`, `clone.go` | `jobFrame`, footer; clone open → `clone.setRun(clone.run, Frame)`, else `updateTableRows()` |
| filebrowser | `update.go`, `jobs.go` | footer only |
| templates | `update.go`, `scan.go` | footer only |
| dashboard | `model.go` | footer only |

```go
// FrameMsg says the animation moved: the spinner frame, the blink phase, or both.
// It carries no snapshot — ChangedMsg is for changes of the registry. The router
// sends it to the view on screen only, on every tick and when a view enters.
type FrameMsg struct {
    Frame         string // bare, Rule 122 (a cell measures it)
    RenderedFrame string // styled, Rule 128 (a footer takes it)
    Blink         bool   // true = ● ; pinned true with app.motion: static or no chain
}
```

No view calls `SetBlinkPhase` yet (no `IndicatorColumn` in any view; A-06 adds the first).

**Tests (write first), one or two per package, named alike:**
- `TestAFrameMovesTheRowSpinner` (workspaces, security, oci_resources, jobsview,
  explorer tree and clone list): a running target, `ChangedMsg{Runs}` then
  `FrameMsg{Frame: "X"}` → the row's cell shows `X`; a second `FrameMsg{Frame: "Y"}` →
  `Y`, runs unchanged.
- `TestAFrameMovesTheFooterSpinner` (workspaces, jobsview, explorer, filebrowser,
  templates, dashboard): a running run, `FrameMsg{RenderedFrame: "R"}` → `RenderFooter`
  contains `R`.
- `TestAFrameKeepsTheSnapshot` (one package suffices, workspaces): `FrameMsg` does not
  reset `m.jobs`/failures held from the last `ChangedMsg`.

**Done when:** `go test ./internal/jobs/ ./internal/ui/workspaces/ ./internal/ui/security/
./internal/ui/oci_resources/ ./internal/ui/jobsview/ ./internal/ui/forge/explorer/
./internal/ui/filebrowser/ ./internal/ui/templates/ ./internal/ui/dashboard/` passes.

## Step 3 — the router chain renamed "animation"; the tick sends `FrameMsg` only · M · after 1 and 2

**Files:** `internal/app/animation.go` (chain moved out of `jobs.go`), `internal/app/jobs.go`,
`internal/app/app.go` (fields, `case`), `internal/app/command_line.go` (`switchView`),
`internal/jobs/message.go` (drop `Frame`/`RenderedFrame` from `ChangedMsg`, rewrite its
comment), the eight `handleJobsChanged` (drop their frame lines — the compiler lists
them), tests: `internal/app/jobs_test.go`, `failures_test.go`, `forge_index_test.go`
(`jobSpinnerInterval` → `animationFastInterval`), and the view tests that put `Frame`
in a `ChangedMsg` (`jobsview_test.go` ×4, `security_jobs_test.go` ×2,
`explorer/model_test.go` ×2, `dashboard_test.go`, `oci_resources/jobs_test.go`,
`workspaces_test.go`) → send a `FrameMsg` instead.

Renames (D2): `jobTickMsg` → `animationTickMsg{seq int; at time.Time}`, `ensureJobTick`
→ `ensureTick`, `handleJobTick` → `handleAnimationTick`, `jobTick` → `animationTick`,
`jobFrame` → `animationFrame`, fields `jobFrameIdx/jobTickSeq/jobTicking` →

```go
// animation is the one chain that moves anything on a row (D5, renamed D2).
type animationState struct {
    seq      int           // identifies the live chain; a tick from another is dropped
    ticking  bool
    interval time.Duration // cadence of the live chain
    frameIdx int
    blinkOn  bool          // starts true (newWithSize); true whenever no chain runs
}

// animationEvery is tea.Every, a var so tests record the interval and inject the time
// without sleeping. Never captured by a Cmd with `a` (Rule 110): seq and interval by value.
var animationEvery = tea.Every

func animationTick(seq int, d time.Duration) tea.Cmd   // animationEvery(d, func(t) { return animationTickMsg{seq, t} })
func (a *App) frameMsg() jobs.FrameMsg                  // frame bare + styled + a.anim.blinkOn
func (a *App) sendFrameTo(target command.ViewType) tea.Cmd // like sendJobsTo, no resize
```

In this step `ensureTick` still keys on `Running() > 0` only, at `animationFastInterval`
(behaviour of today). `handleAnimationTick`: stale seq → `nil`; `Running()==0` → stop;
else `frameIdx++` and `tea.Batch(a.sendFrameTo(a.currentView), animationTick(seq, d))` —
**no `broadcastJobs()` on a tick any more**. `switchView` batches `sendJobsTo(view)` then
`sendFrameTo(view)`. `jobsChanged()` = `broadcastJobs()` + `sendFrameTo(a.currentView)` +
`ensureTick()`.

**Tests (write first; existing ones renamed where they cover the same thing):**
- `TestOnlyOneAnimationChainIsEverAlive` (was `TestOnlyOneSpinnerChainIsEverAlive`).
- `TestATickFromAnOlderChainIsDropped` (kept, on `animationTickMsg`): no frame change,
  `cmd == nil`, no `FrameMsg` delivered.
- `TestATickSendsAFrameAndNoSnapshot`: two held fake views, a run; after a tick the view
  on screen got exactly one more `FrameMsg` and no new `ChangedMsg`; the other got
  nothing.
- `TestTheFrameIsBareAndItsRenderingIsNot` (was `…BroadcastFrame…`, now on `FrameMsg`).
- `TestAViewEnteringTheScreenGetsTheSnapshotAndTheFrame`: `switchView` → the view
  receives a `ChangedMsg` then a `FrameMsg` whose `Blink == a.anim.blinkOn`.
- `TestARegistryChangeStillReachesEveryView` (existing broadcast test, adapted): a
  `StartMsg` → every held view gets a `ChangedMsg`; the view on screen also a `FrameMsg`.
- `TestTheChainRunsWhileWorkDoesAndRestartsAfterwards` (kept, adapted: asserts a
  `FrameMsg` instead of a second snapshot).

**Done when:** `go build ./...` and `go test ./internal/app/ ./internal/jobs/ ./internal/ui/...`
pass; `grep -rn "\.RenderedFrame\|msg\.Frame" internal/ui` only hits `FrameMsg` handlers.

## Step 4 — `BlinkingView`, the `Update` wrapper, the two cadences, `motionStatic` · M · after 3

**Files:** `internal/app/app.go` (interface, wrapper, `motionStatic`), `internal/app/animation.go`,
`internal/app/harness_test.go` (comment listing probed interfaces; a `blinkingView` fake:
`fakeView` + `wants bool`), new `internal/app/animation_router_test.go`.

```go
// BlinkingView is implemented by a view with a row that blinks for a reason the
// registry does not know: an instant action (busy), an agent running, a group's
// children loading. Asked after every Update — a level, not an edge (R3).
type BlinkingView interface {
    WantsBlink() bool
}

// Update is the router's only entry: the dispatch, then the level check of the
// animation chain. update is today's switch, unchanged.
func (a *App) Update(msg tea.Msg) (tea.Model, tea.Cmd) {
    model, cmd := a.update(msg)
    return model, tea.Batch(cmd, a.ensureTick())
}

func (a *App) wantsBlink() bool          // view on screen implements BlinkingView && WantsBlink()
func (a *App) setMotionStatic(on bool)   // A-02 calls it; true pins blinkOn and stops blink-only chains
```

`ensureTick`: `d, ok := cadence(a.jobs.Running() > 0, a.wantsBlink(), a.motionStatic)`;
`!ok` → `nil`; `ticking && interval <= d` → `nil`; else `seq++`, `ticking = true`,
`interval = d`, return `animationTick(seq, d)` (replaces a slower chain: criterion 3).
`handleAnimationTick`: cadence `!ok` → `ticking = false`; if `!blinkOn` → `blinkOn = true`
and `sendFrameTo(currentView)` (a row is never left on `○`); else frame advances only when
`Running() > 0`, `blinkOn = motionStatic || blinkPhase(msg.at)`, `interval = d`, FrameMsg to
the view on screen, renew at `d` (downgrade 100 → 500 happens here, no new seq).

func TestMeasureRedrawCost(t *testing.T)

line per case: `rows=20 mode=blink bytes/s=…`.

```
1 ──┐
    ├─> 3 ─> 4 ─> 5
2 ──┘          └─> 6 (Q1)      7 last
```
Step 2 splits into eight independent view sub-steps.

| Risk | Level | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|

| Off-screen views hold a stale frame | low | by design; `switchView` sends the frame on entry; context switch goes through `jobsChanged` |
| `tea.Every` creates its timer when the Cmd is built, not when run | low | a dropped Cmd leaks one timer until it fires (buffered channel, collected); the stub hides it in tests |
| Redraw cost H2 higher than assumed over SSH (line-level rewrite, styled lines) | unknown | measured in step 6; the A-06 checkpoint decides, `app.motion: static` exists from A-02 |
| `ChangedMsg` shape change | low | internal type; every sender is the router. Not irreversible |
